title: Mumbai's Jiniya Chatterjee Wins Rs 9.6 Lakh as Wakefit Sleep Champion
excerpt: A singer and entrepreneur from Mumbai out-slept nine finalists over 60 tracked nights to win Season 5 of Wakefit's Sleep Internship, which drew nearly two lakh applications — and pre-registrations for Season 6 are already open.
body:
• Jiniya Chatterjee of Mumbai was crowned Sleep Champion of Wakefit's Sleep Internship Season 5, winning Rs 9.6 lakh and a sponsored vacation.
  • The contest drew nearly two lakh applications; 10 interns were selected to sleep at home for 60 consecutive nights on a Wakefit mattress, tracked nightly with a target of about nine hours.
  • Every intern who finished received Rs 1 lakh; the champion was decided in a reality-show-style finale on final sleep scores after challenges including a memory-based bedroom setup and a sleep auction.
  • Across five seasons the program has taken more than 10 lakh applications; pre-registrations for Season 6 are open on Wakefit's website.

The best-rested person in India this Diwali season may be Jiniya Chatterjee. The Mumbai singer, performer and entrepreneur has been crowned Sleep Champion of Season 5 of Wakefit's Sleep Internship, winning Rs 9.6 lakh and a sponsored vacation after 60 consecutive nights of tracked, scored sleep.

Wakefit, the Bengaluru-based sleep products company, launched the Sleep Internship in 2019 as part marketing, part sleep evangelism. This season drew nearly two lakh applications. After screening rounds and personal interviews, 10 interns were chosen — from Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Chandigarh, Raipur, Panaji and Dehradun. Each slept at home, in their own bed, on a Wakefit mattress, with a sleep tracker recording nightly scores against a target of about nine hours a night. A public leaderboard tracked the standings, and every intern who completed the 60 days received Rs 1 lakh.

How the champion was decided

Sleeping was only part of the contest. Weekly creative challenges named a "Pro Sleeper of the Week" — tasks included recreating famous movie scenes with a sleep angle and slipping the words "blanket" or "pillow" into conversations undetected. The leaderboard's top three were Ratnagiri Manikandan, Chatterjee and Mehek Khot, with Hyderabad's Karim Khan joining as a fourth finalist after winning the most weekly challenges.

The finale, staged as a reality-show event called "Big Bedd," added a Memory Foam Challenge — recreating a reference bedroom setup from memory — and a Sleep Auction, in which finalists bid a limited pool of points for pillows, blankets, air-conditioning control, lighting and sound. The championship came down to a close comparison of the final night's sleep scores, and Chatterjee won Rs 9.6 lakh against a headline prize of up to Rs 10 lakh. Wakefit's own winners page describes her as a performer since the age of three who runs her own business and "fiercely protects her bedtime" — planning her schedule, avoiding caffeine and guarding her sleep time.

"At Wakefit, we have always believed that good sleep is fundamental to a healthy, balanced life. With the Sleep Internship, we wanted to take this conversation beyond the bedroom."

— Chaitanya Ramalingegowda, Director and Co-founder, Wakefit

Across its first four seasons, the program took more than 10 lakh applications and paid 65 interns Rs 1 lakh stipends each; past champions include a civil services aspirant who scored 91.36 and an auditor who recorded 99% sleep efficiency. Pre-registrations for Season 6 are open on Wakefit's Sleep Internship page. The contest is a promotion, not a health study — but its premise lands because the problem is real: nine hours a night, protected for 60 days, is something almost none of its two lakh applicants currently get.
